description.narrative:
The overall objective of UN Multi Partner Trust Fund is to support the construction of peace in Colombia, contributing to the implementation of the Peace Agreement agreed between the Colombian Government and the former FARC-EP in 2016, as well as other actions related to peace building established by the National Government.
The fund's theory of change considers the context and address the root causes of the conflict, particularly in remote rural areas of the country with a historical weak institutional presence and capacity. A third phase of the fund was approved by the Steering Committee in June 2023.
The theory of change of the third phase consists of five thematic areas, each with its own objectives:
1) Sustainable human development: to promote comprehensive rural reform, rural development and human security with the objective of closing historical gaps, reducing inequality and strengthening security.
Under this area, a sub-area is included that seeks to support the national Government in the implementation of the Comprehensive Action against Antipersonnel Mines (AICMA).
2) Reincorporation: to strengthen the reintegration route of the ex-combatants, under a sustainability approach and in this way promote their effective inclusion in social dynamics, political and economic aspects of civil life, encouraging coexistence, reconciliation and not stigmatization.
3) Victim's rights and transitional justice: to support initiatives in line with the system set up in the peace agreement on Justice, Truth, Reparation and no Repetition.
4) Communication: to constant follow-up of the fund with a permanent, efficient and transparent communication.
5) Peace building beyond the 2016 Agreement: to support on-going and possible future peace negotiations as well as support initiatives to reduce violence, promote peace building, trust, and participation of communities and civil society.
The specific objectives for each of these areas are explained in greater detail in the Terms of Reference and Manual of operations of the fund.

Sida's bidrag till FN:s fredsfond för Colombia. Fonden ger bidrag till insatser för stabilisering förtroendeskapande samt genomförandet av fredsavtalet mellan den colombianska regeringen och FARC, i syfte att: 1. Öka lokalbefolkningens förtroende för statliga institutioner på nationell och lokal nivå. 2. Öka människors och i synnerhet offren och / medborgares förtroende för fredsprocessen i de områden som drabbats hårdast av konflikten. 3. Förhindra och/eller minska brott och våld i samband med utbrott av väpnade konflikter och demobiliseringsprocesser. 4. Hantera konfliktsituationer på lokal nivå genom tidiga insatser (rapid response). 5. Bidra till att skapa fredsvinster, konkreta positiva förbättringar för människors dagliga liv, inom områdena säkerhet, rättvisa och utveckling. Andra givare till fonden inkluderar Canada, Irland, Norge, Storbritannien, Tyskland, och Schweiz.

The support to the UN multi-partner Trust Fund for Colombia ("contribution to specific-purpose programmes and funds") promotes actions for stabilisation, building trust, and the implementation of the Peace Agreement between the Colombian government and FARC. The Fund intends to address the root causes of the conflict, particularly in remote rural areas of the country. The Fund works within four thematic areas: 1) Stabilization; 2) Reincorporation; 3) Victim's rights and transitional justice; 4) Communication.

description.narrative:
To date (latest information received on 3 June 2023), the fund has received a total of USD 224.8M in contributions, including interest. USD 181M have been allocated, of which 43% has been allocated to gender. The fund has approved a total of 276 projects, reaching approximately 2.2 million beneficiaries in 598 municipalities. Since start, 41% of the beneficiaries has been men, 51% women, 4% boys and 4% girls. In terms of geographical coverage, the fund has continued to concentrate its support to the 170 most severely conflict-affected municipalities prioritized by the national government through the special territorial development plans (so called PDETs).
According to the Annual Report for 2022, the interventions during 2022 focused mainly on comprehensive development with the purpose of closing the inequality gaps in the most marginalized territories and guaranteeing their security. They also focused on strengthening the capacities of victims and the Transitional Justice System. In addition, work was done on the reincorporation of the ex-combatants and reconciliation was promoted.
To date, within the fund´s pillars, Sustainable human development continues to be the area with the largest number of projects and highest level of funding, just as previous years. This pillar represents 47,4% of total funding, followed by Victims and Reincorporation (25% and 15,7% respectively). The area of Communications is purposely much smaller, representing 7,4% of total funding.
During 2022, the fund supported (directly) 88 implementing civil society organizations, of which 42 were new organizations that joined during the year.
During 2022 the fund has supported several key processes, of which some examples worth mentioning are the following:
- 2022 was a difficult year for human rights defenders in the country, according to the 2022 OHCHR report, "256 allegations of homicides of human rights defenders were received, of which 116 were verified as a link between their death and their work defending human rights" (https://www.hchr.org.co/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Informe-Anual-2022-en-castellano.pdf). The fund reiterated its commitment to the safety of leaders, through important allocations not only to strengthen the institutions in charge of ensuring their safety, but also to strengthen, through civil society, protection and self-protection mechanisms.
- In June 2022, the final report of the Truth Commission was delivered to Colombian society, and the Follow-up and Monitoring Committee of the recommendations of the Final Report was formed, both supported by the fund. The fund also prioritized the Legacy of the Commission, directly supporting civil society organizations to disseminate the content of the report and appropriate the findings and recommendations to the territories.
- By December 2022, the JEP (Special Jurisdiction for Peace) had given priority to 11 cases, with 10 of them still ongoing. They had conducted 300 hearings, which are crucial spaces for transitional justice, contributing significantly to the pursuit of truth, acknowledgement of past events, and reconciliation. The fund supported over 3,000 victims to participate in voluntary testimonies for macro cases 03, 05, and 06. It also bolstered the investigation and prosecution chambers, expediting the documentation and analysis of cases. Furthermore, the fund provided support for the first hearing on sexual and gender violence for case 005, which is assessed to have contributed to the prioritization of a new macro case (case 11) focused on sexual violence. This milestone aligns with the implementation of Resolution 1325 and the rights of women victims.
